verdict_a_acceptance.basis: The unintegrated case follows the real Profile UI and owned-write journal, checks a visible failed-save state, retries through the actual Save control, rereads after reopening, and attempts restoration. It has not run in the native panel. Its receipt covers only member/warm while the inventory also names reload. These are source capabilities, not native acceptance evidence.
missing: Native execution with a receipt showing the intended member's POST was the failed request and the owned row was absent again after runner cleanup.
The inventory's reload failure and retry branch is not represented by this warm-only case.

findings.finding: The fault matches only origin, route and POST. It does not check the verified owner ID, organization, or request body, and fails every matching POST until disabled. A concurrent or unexpected profile write can be denied instead of the intended Save. The count check detects a second denial only afterward; it cannot undo that denial. Scope the fault to the intended owner's upsert and fail exactly one matching request.

If Fetch.disable rejects, stop removes the sole requestPaused listener anyway. CDP interception can remain enabled, leaving later matching reads paused with nobody to continue them; journal reconciliation and the runner's owned-row cleanup can then hang or lose restoration. Preserve a working continuation or recover the Fetch domain before detaching the handler, and make failure explicit.

The case records original_restored=true when no retry write was observed even if cleanup only discarded the local draft. For the owned first-save row, the outer runner's exact conditional deletion is the actual original-absence restoration. The local receipt should distinguish draft discard or value restoration from verified row absence so it cannot imply complete restoration before outer cleanup succeeds.

positive_evidence: The failed-save observation uses the real panel's Preferred input, visible error, dirty state, and enabled Save; retry and restore go through journal.save and the UI, with server rereads in journal reconciliation.
The case receipt carries booleans, not Preferred values; syntax and targeted Biome checks pass.
